artworks.title: Studies of Achilles for "Chiron and Achilles"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image displays a sketch of a male figure shown primarily from the chest up. One arm is raised beside his head, and the other is in a downward flexed position. The figure's head is turned to the side, with faint indications of facial features such as the structure of his jaw and the outline of his nose. He has short, closely cropped hair. The figure's midsection is visible, revealing pronounced musculature and subtle lines hinting at abdominal definition. The figure appears unclothed, with no visible accessories or objects. The background is plain and unadorned, highlighting the focus on the body's anatomy.

artworks.title: Study for "Frieze of Prophets"
artworks.medium: charcoal and white chalk on gray laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of draped fabric or clothing on a concealed form. The image features a cascading arrangement of fabric or garments, suggesting the outline of layers enveloped around an unseen structure. The use of shading and line work creates depth and texture.

artworks.title: Study for "Apollo and Daphne"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image is a sketch depicting a full-body view of a nude person seen from the back. The individual is standing on their toes with their arms raised above their head, both hands pressing against an invisible surface. The person's head is tilted slightly upward, emphasizing the neck and shoulder lines. The facial features are minimally detailed with a focus on the profile, and the hair appears to be shaved or very short. The background is a plain, unadorned surface, with no detailed elements or objects besides the focus on the figure. There are no visible pieces of jewelry or objects being held.

artworks.title: Studies for "The Unveiling of Truth"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a figure in a kneeling position, viewed from the back. The individual has their left knee on the ground and the right knee raised, with both arms extended upwards and slightly outwards. Short hair is sketched following the contour of the head. The figure does not have any clothing depicted. In the background, on the right side, there is a detailed sketch of a person's head from the back, focusing on the flow of wavy hair. The background is a plain, textured paper.

artworks.title: Study for "Apollo and the Muses"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image features an oval shape containing a series of curved and flowing lines that form an abstract arrangement of figures. The central figure is raised, with arms outstretched, surrounded by other figures in various poses. These figures, interconnected by continuous lines, draw associations with a scene of celebration or ritual.

artworks.title: Study for "Phaethon"
artworks.medium: graphite and charcoal on brown laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a male figure in a dynamic falling or floating position. The person's facial features display a profile with closed eyes and a calm expression. The figure is depicted as nude, showcasing detailed musculature. The background features swirls resembling clouds or smoke against a brown paper backdrop.

artworks.title: Studies of Notus for "The Winds"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures and three hands grasping spherical objects. The drawing depicts abstract figures with softened facial features and muscular body outlines. Both figures appear to be male and are in dynamic postures. One figure is holding an oversized vessel. Additionally, there are three separate studies of hands grasping spherical objects. The piece highlights contour lines and shadowing, emphasizing form and volume.

artworks.title: Study of Apollo for "Apollo and the Muses"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image depicts a person in a standing position. The person's left arm is raised and slightly bent at the elbow, with the right hand on the hip. The facial features are subtly outlined, showing a strong jawline and a calm expression, with short, dark hair neatly styled. The person is partially draped in fabric covering the lower body. The upper body is bare, showing musculature. There are no visible objects or jewelry. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Studies of Oxen
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: Two detailed sketches of oxen are positioned in the center of the image. One ox faces forward while the other is oriented towards the right. The drawing has a monochromatic color palette of black linework on a beige background. Surrounding the central figures are various smaller sketches of oxen heads, horns, a cart, and other related shapes scattered across the page. The sketches are dispersed throughout the sheet, varying in detail and capturing different perspectives and positions of the animals.

artworks.title: Study for "Arion"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body sketch of a seated male figure. He is in a semi-reclined pose with his arms positioned as described. The figure has a serene expression with closed eyes, a defined nose, and short hair. The drawing is minimalistic, showcasing the contours of his body with simple lines and shading. The male figure is nude, and the background is plain.

artworks.title: Studies for "Apollo in His Chariot with the Hours"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows two horse heads in pencil sketch on beige paper. The first horse head is on the left, depicted in profile with detailed features such as the eye, nostril, and mouth. The neck is outlined and blends into the paper. On the right and slightly above, there is a smaller sketch of another horse head in profile looking downward, with shadows emphasizing its features like the eye, nostril, and mouth. Both sketches show musculature and realism. There is no distinct background, with the paper serving as the backdrop for the drawings.

artworks.title: Study for "Philosophy"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a seated person. The person is sitting with one leg slightly raised and the other resting on the ground. They have a muscular build and are leaning forward slightly, with their head turned to one side. Their facial features are outlined with minimal detail, suggesting a concentrated or introspective expression. The individual has short hair and is wearing a large cloak or drape that falls around their shoulders and covers parts of their torso and legs, leaving the chest partially visible. The remaining fabric drapes over their knees to the ground. There is no jewelry or other objects visible. The background is plain and unadorned, emphasizing the figure as the focal point.

artworks.title: Studies for "The Fall of Gog and Magog"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a sketched drawing of two horse heads. Both horses are depicted from the neck up, with slightly different angles and positions. The horse on the left is facing downward, with perked-up ears and a mane. The horse on the right has a slightly raised head, flaring nostrils, and lines suggesting motion or tension. Each horse is outlined with detail, focusing on features like the eyes, nostrils, and muscular structure. The artwork is done in monochromatic tones using charcoal or graphite on a pale surface, creating depth and texture. The background is plain to emphasize the horses.

artworks.title: Study for "Judgment"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image is a charcoal drawing featuring two intertwined figures. The focus is on their muscular backs and limb extents. The figures' heads are visible but lack detailed facial features, with one figure's head turned away and the other's head partially visible. The drawing captures the figures' nude forms, with no clothing depicted. There are no visible objects or jewelry on either figure. The background is a plain, untextured surface.

artworks.title: Study for Figure above "Music"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a person seated on a circular platform or sphere. The person is depicted from head to toes, with one leg bent and the other extended. Their upper body is leaning slightly back, with their left arm raised and right arm resting on the bent knee. The person has a short hairstyle and facial features, including defined cheekbones. They are wearing form-fitting shorts and there is no visible jewelry or objects in their hands. The background is plain, focusing on the figure.

artworks.title: Study of the Resurrection for "Fifteen Mysteries of the Rosary"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image is a charcoal sketch of a person's upper body, including the hips, shoulders, arms, and upper thighs. The individual is posed with a slight twist, emphasizing the torso's musculature. The face is partially visible, with only the outlined chin. The person appears to be nude, with a focus on anatomical structure and form. There are handwritten text at the bottom and sides, including a name, address, and days of the week. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Studies for "Triumph of Religion"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two muscular forearms and hands. The drawing features a detailed study of a forearm and clenched hand in profile, with prominent shading emphasizing the muscular structure. Another hand appears gripping a vertical object. The hands and forearms are depicted with precision, using a combination of soft lines and bold, dark strokes to highlight contours and textures. In the lower right corner, there's handwritten text that appears to be an address or name. The overall style showcases a classical approach to anatomical studies, focusing on the realism and detail of human form.

artworks.title: Forest, Ramsau, Germany
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)

artworks.title: Hintersee, Germany
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This image shows a pencil sketch of a natural landscape with rocky formations and vegetation. There are two main areas: one with large boulders and lush plants to the upper left, and another with detailed bushes and trees to the lower right. The artist uses soft strokes, cross-hatching, and shading to depict texture and shadows. The drawing is done in graphite monochrome, emphasizing the shapes and forms of the landscape. The artwork is signed "Hintersee Aug, 1879" in the lower left corner, and the horizon is not shown in the composition.

artworks.title: Olimpio Fusco
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: Drawn with tones of gray and black with charcoal on cream-white paper, a young man’s cleanshaven face floats near the top of the sheet. He faces and looks directly at us with his head tipped slightly back. His dark eyes are shaded under dark brows. His upper lip is full, and his mouth is closed in a set line. His thick, dark, slightly unruly hair sweeps back from his forehead, and he has a squared chin line. The lines indicating his neck fade where they would meet his shoulders. The work is inscribed with charcoal under the man’s head, near the bottom of the sheet: “Olimpio Fusco 63A Aspinlea Rd Hammersmith.”

artworks.title: Study for "The Fall of Gog and Magog"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural column capital. The drawing shows the top view of the capital with a round, circular top featuring six radial lines. The capital displays intricate carvings including volutes and vertical grooves suggesting fluting. The shading and line work emphasize the three-dimensional form of the object.

artworks.title: Back of a Man with Pole
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image is a sketch showing an upper body view of a person from behind. The person appears to be standing with their torso slightly bent forward and their head turned slightly to the left. The individual's facial features are not visible. They are wearing a wide-brimmed hat, a short-sleeved shirt, and their right arm is bent as if they are holding an object over their right shoulder. The background is plain and unembellished.

artworks.title: Studies of Victory for "Death and Victory"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)

artworks.title: Study of Field Marshal John French for "General Officers of World War I"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
